question: How long do created marshes take to reach biodiversity and function comparable to natural reference wetlands, and which attributes lag?
text: No included study reports how long a created marsh takes to match a natural one, and each comparison below is a snapshot at one age, not a recovery path. Created and restored marshes had lower growth, size and biomass than natural marshes, with high certainty. Species richness was lower in two of three studies, with moderate certainty. Plant cover and survival were also lower, but each rests on a single study, with very low and low certainty. Single studies found higher abundance and reproduction, mixed animal abundance and an unclear difference in community composition, all with very low certainty. As marshes aged, studies found no clear change in community composition, with moderate certainty, or in species richness and invasive species, with very low certainty. No included study compared created and natural marshes on ecosystem processes, hydrology, soil properties, soil and water chemistry, contaminants, plant establishment, animal behaviour or invasive species.
